paper_id: Yang et al. - 2013 - From RSSI to CSI Indoor localization via channel response
title: From RSSI to CSI: Indoor localization via channel response
motivation: RSSI suffers dramatic performance degradation due to multipath fading and temporal dynamics, limiting indoor localization to room-level accuracy
problem_framing: Survey paper that classifies existing CSI-based localization works into three categories based on how channel response is used
key_insight: Channel response is to RSSI what a rainbow is to a sunbeam - it separates multipath components that RSSI superimposes
method_signature: Survey classifying CSI usage into power-based, time/angle estimation, and human detection categories
evaluation_criteria: Localization accuracy (submeter vs room-level), ranging error, fingerprinting precision
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: The time resolution remains only sufficient to distinguish path clusters rather than individual multipath components due to limited WiFi bandwidth
evidence_for_taste: RSSI is the superimposition of multipath signals with fast changing phases
Channel response is to RSSI what a rainbow (color spectrum) is to a sunbeam
fundamentally bounds the number of resolvable paths
theoretical solutions numerically unstable without practical constraints
large shadowing Xσ blurs the monotonic trend
thinking_moves: 从物理层视角解释RSSI失效的根因：叠加相位导致信息湮灭
将通道响应类比棱镜分光，强调信息解耦而非降噪
按使用方式对文献做分类而非按技术路线，揭示不同路径的认知差异
承认技术限制：带宽不足导致只能分辨路径簇而非单条路径
